_doc: Every constant is {value, source}. A Test Card may set its own thresholds, but they are frozen with the card; nothing is changed after data arrives.

importance_scale.source: Assumptions map (Bland & Osterwalder, Testing Business Ideas): importance axis; five-point scale chosen for scoring.

evidence_scale.source: Assumptions map evidence axis; 0 = none, 5 = strong behavioural evidence (deposit/pre-sale).

critical_importance_min.source: Design default: assumptions rated 4-5 on importance are critical (top half of the importance axis).

experiments_per_round.source: Design default: test the three riskiest assumptions in parallel, then re-plan.

min_solutions.source: Torres, Opportunity Solution Tree: generate at least three solutions per target opportunity to avoid fixating on one.

planning_half_width.source: Design default precision for smoke tests (+/-5 percentage points); n = z^2 p(1-p)/h^2 (10% +/- 5pp gives 139).

min_visitors_floor.source: Design floor so tiny tests are never judged; research-methods track recommends 150-200 targeted visitors per variant.

odi_min_n.source: Ulwick / Strategyn: ODI surveys use 180-1,200 respondents.

odi_top_two_box.source: Ulwick: importance and satisfaction are the share rating 4 or 5 on a 1-5 scale, divided by 10.

kano_min_n.source: Chapman & Callegaro (Google): Kano category assignment may be unreliable below about 200 respondents.

kano_tie_order.source: Conventional Kano tie-break: Must-be > One-dimensional > Attractive > Indifferent.

vw_min_n.source: Practitioner consensus of 100-200 respondents per segment (not verified against a primary source).

nms_calibration.source: Newton, Miller & Smith 1993 purchase-likelihood calibration as used by Sawtooth defaults.

ellis_threshold.source: Sean Ellis: 40% 'very disappointed' indicates product-market fit.

ellis_min_n.source: Ellis / Vohra: about 40 responses give directional results.

min_interviews.source: Ash Maurya, Running Lean: at least 10 good problem interviews.

gnc_base.source: Guest, Namey & Chen 2020: base size 4 interviews.

min_positives_per_code.source: Design default for small interview samples (lower than the desk default of 5).

id_prefix.source: Interview records are numbered IV-000001 so they never collide with discovery evidence ids (EV-).

value.label: Fragmentation
value.definition: The person juggles several tools or places to get one job done; there is no single place.
value.include: Mentions switching between tools, copying data between apps, or many tools for one job.
value.exclude: A single tool lacking one feature (use a pain or feature code).

value.label: Integration missing
value.definition: Tools the person uses do not connect or sync with each other.
value.include: No integration, broken sync, manual export/import between named tools.
value.exclude: General complaints about a tool's own features.

value.label: Price mismatch
value.definition: Too expensive for the value received or for this segment.
value.include: Explicit cost complaints, seat pricing that does not fit, no small tier.
value.exclude: Statements about willingness to pay without complaint (use stance wtp).

value.label: Too complex
value.definition: The product is too complex or heavy for this user or use case.
value.include: Bloat, steep learning curve, built for bigger teams.

value.label: Language or locale missing
value.definition: Language, currency, tax, date format or local compliance is not supported.
value.include: Translation gaps, missing local currency or tax rules, regional regulation.

value.label: Support gap
value.definition: Support is missing, slow or unhelpful.
value.include: Unanswered tickets, no human support, slow responses.

value.label: Reliability
value.definition: The product breaks, loses data or is unavailable.
value.include: Bugs, data loss, outages, failed syncs.

value.label: Pain grows with volume
value.definition: The pain grows as usage, volume, clients or team size grow (dose-response).
value.include: 'Fine at 5 clients, impossible at 50', costs scaling with volume.
value.exclude: Pain that is constant regardless of volume.

value.label: Push of the situation
value.definition: Something in the current situation pushes the person to seek change.
value.include: Frustration events, deadlines missed, a breaking point.
value.exclude: Attraction to a specific new product (use F-PULL).

value.label: Pull of the new solution
value.definition: An attraction to a new way of doing the job.
value.include: 'I saw X does Y and wanted that', promised outcomes.
value.exclude: Complaints about the old way (use F-PUSH).

value.label: Anxiety of the new
value.definition: Worries that hold back switching to a new solution.
value.include: Migration risk, learning cost, fear it will not work.
value.exclude: Satisfaction with the current tool (use F-HABIT).

value.label: Habit of the present
value.definition: Comfort with the current way that holds back switching.
value.include: 'Good enough', 'we have always used', sunk cost.
value.exclude: Fears about the new tool (use F-ANX).

value.label: First thought
value.definition: The moment the person first realised the current way is not good enough.

value.label: Active looking
value.definition: Actively searching, comparing and trialling options.
value.include: Trials, comparisons, demo requests, 'looking for an alternative'.

value.label: Deciding
value.definition: Choosing and committing, including what tipped the decision.

value.label: Consuming
value.definition: Experience after switching: onboarding, first value, regret or delight.

standard_codes.source: Same standard X-/F-/T- codes as market-gap-discovery (coding.standard_codes): cross-cutting pains, Forces of Progress and the switch timeline (Moesta & Spiek). Used to build validation/codebook.json for standalone ideas.

evidence_ladder.source: Testing Business Ideas evidence strength (doing over saying); ordering click < email < booked call < LOI < deposit/pre-sale from the market-methods track. Desk evidence (search demand) and prototypes (technical spikes) sit below behavioural evidence.

viability_min_level.source: Design default: a viability (willingness-to-pay) assumption counts as validated only with LOI-level evidence or stronger, or a Van Westendorp range that contains the planned price with n >= vw_min_n.

desirability_min_level.source: Design default: desirability needs at least email-level behaviour (a waitlist sign-up), not clicks or opinions alone.

precedence.source: Design rule: when critical assumptions disagree, the most conservative pre-registered action wins.

retention_days.source: GDPR storage limitation; delete raw respondent data after the decision.

store_emails_in_repo.source: Emails stay in the human-controlled form service; only aggregates enter the run folder.

demand_strength.source: Testing Business Ideas: evidence strength rises with doing over saying and money over email; mapping used by the validation cards (V10).
